analysis: Isoniazid (INH), a commonly used antitubercular medication, is known to cause peripheral neuropathy as a side effect. This neuropathy is primarily due to the interference of INH with the metabolism of pyridoxine (vitamin B6), leading to a deficiency. The standard medical treatment for preventing or treating INH-induced neuropathy involves the supplementation of pyridoxine. This approach is well-supported by medical literature and clinical practice, aligning with the consensus that pyridoxine supplementation can effectively restore normal nerve function and alleviate symptoms of neuropathy caused by INH. Other vitamins listed, such as Thiamine, Niacin, and Riboflavin, do not directly address the specific mechanism by which INH induces neuropathy.
